role: Master Thesis Proposal: TinyML for Predictive Maintenance in Embedded Systems
key_responsibilities: Develop embedded software for real-time system control, fault injection, and synchronized data acquisition
Implement configurable, reproducible fault conditions at varying severity
Build a labeled dataset of normal and faulty operation
Train ML models in Python and deploy them on a resource-constrained microcontroller
Evaluate accuracy vs memory vs compute vs latency vs energy trade-offs
Apply quantization, pruning and knowledge distillation
Map detected faults to maintenance actions

strengths: Real-time embedded control with synchronized acquisition is directly evidenced: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor (timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, low-level I2C driver, deterministic 1 Hz, 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM) is almost exactly the 'embedded software for real-time control and synchronized data acquisition' task.

Building the controllable electromechanical test rig is covered end-to-end: Robocon holonomic drive (quadrature decoding from a 4-bit A/B state machine on hardware interrupts, 15 kHz PWM via DuePWM, closed-loop heading correction from encoder odometry) plus EAGLE PCB fabrication and SolidWorks.

Quantization depth is unusually strong for a thesis applicant: QAT project implements straight-through-estimator fake quantization, int8 symmetric weights / uint8 activations, EMA activation-scale observer frozen for the final 25% of training, folded into a fixed-point requantization multiplier and shift, with integer-only inference at 97.43% on MNIST.

The accuracy / memory / latency trade-off evaluation the thesis asks for is a repeated pattern in his work: SLM compression (~55% VRAM reduction at <1% accuracy loss and +0.09 perplexity, profiled with pynvml and psutil) and CUDA VGG16 kernels (49.2 ms coalesced vs 73.3 ms uncoalesced vs 77.5 ms CPU).

Labeled-dataset construction is backed by more than one project: CARLA auto-generation of ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 UFLD frames with zero manual annotation, Tusk's 1,133-image annotated detection set, and the LeRobot-structured multi-camera capture pipeline in COFFIN.

Required stack is fully met with depth, not mentions: C/C++ (bare-metal STM32, Arduino IK, CUDA C++), Python (PyTorch, HF, Cython backend), microcontrollers (STM32 Cortex-M4, Arduino Due, Nano), Git/GitLab.
Sensor-combination studies have a real analogue: COFFIN's camera range-gate plus dual VL53L0X ToF over a TCA9548A I2C mux, where the sensing mix itself was the design decision.
real_gaps: Predictive maintenance, condition monitoring and fault diagnosis as a domain is entirely absent from the profile — no vibration analysis, no bearing/motor fault signatures, no RUL or health-indicator work.

No ML model has ever run on a microcontroller. All edge deployment is Jetson-class (TensorRT, YOLO); the Tusk TFLite/ONNX export targeted mobile, and the QAT int8 export went to a hex .mem file rather than an MCU runtime. TFLite Micro, CMSIS-NN, Edge Impulse and microTVM are all unused.

Fault injection — designing configurable, reproducible faults at graded severity — has no backing. The nearest thing is the Robocon fail-safe state machine on controller disconnect and the 11 integration failures debugged in COFFIN, neither of which is deliberate fault synthesis.
Pruning appears in the profile's self-described strongest areas but no bullet anywhere demonstrates it. Knowledge distillation has no backing at all.

Energy consumption is one of the five trade-off axes the thesis names, and it is the one axis he has never measured — his profiling is memory, latency and throughput (pynvml, psutil, FPS, Flash/RAM), never joules or current draw.

Time-series / signal classification on sensor streams is thin. Depth exists in vision and speech; the closest sensor-stream work is the ADXL345 z-axis differential tap-detection threshold, which is hand-rolled rather than learned.
Mapping diagnosed faults to maintenance actions is a reliability-engineering layer with nothing comparable in the profile.

Eligibility, stated as prose rather than scored: the posting wants a final-year master's student registering a 30 ECTS thesis. He finished the M.S. in May 2026, so there is no enrolling university behind the application.
overstated_by_keywords: Pruning — counted as Have off the strongest_areas line, but no project bullet demonstrates it.
TinyML — the Have/Adjacent credit rests on Jetson TensorRT and a mobile TFLite export, which is a different compute class from a Cortex-M microcontroller with kilobytes of RAM.
Energy consumption profiling — credited as adjacent to pynvml GPU power work, but no power or energy figure appears anywhere in the profile.
Fault detection / classification — credited via CNN and object-detection classifiers, which share the ML machinery but none of the fault-signature or sensor-stream specifics.
understated_by_keywords: The QAT project is the single most relevant thing in the profile for this thesis and the keyword pass reduced it to 'quantization'. Exporting int8 weights as a 17,024-entry hex .mem file with scale parameters and 100 golden test vectors, with fixed-point requantization matching the float reference on 99.996% of hidden values, is MCU/FPGA-grade integer deployment engineering.
The STM32 temperature monitor's reported 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM footprint shows he already thinks in the memory budget TinyML lives in.

Automated dataset generation in CARLA (semantic segmentation plus raycast occlusion filtering, zero manual annotation) is directly transferable to generating a labeled normal-vs-fault dataset at graded severity.
Digital Signal Processing and Random Signal Analysis coursework plus the ADXL345 tap-detection work give a sensor-signal foundation the keyword pass scored only as 'signal processing'.
screening_gaps: Not an enrolled student. The posting is a 30 ECTS master's thesis for two final-year students, and a thesis has to be registered against a home university; he graduated in May 2026. This is not a weak-fit concern, it is an eligibility bar, and it ends the application regardless of the skill match.

Never deployed a model on a microcontroller. The thesis's second half is TinyML on a resource-constrained MCU, and every edge deployment in the profile is Jetson-class; no TFLite Micro, CMSIS-NN or Edge Impulse anywhere.

No predictive maintenance, condition monitoring or vibration-analysis background, and no fault-injection or knowledge-distillation experience — the thesis's subject matter and two of its named optimization techniques.
llm_analysis.reasoning: On pure skill and domain fit this is one of the better-matched postings he has seen: the embedded half (bare-metal real-time control, timer-synchronized acquisition, encoder/PWM motor control, PCB work) and the model-compression half (QAT with integer-only inference, int8 LLM quantization, memory and latency trade-off benchmarking) are both genuinely his, and the required stack is met with depth rather than mentions. The honest gaps are that TinyML has never actually touched a microcontroller for him, and the predictive-maintenance domain plus fault injection, pruning, distillation and energy measurement are unevidenced. The decisive problem is structural rather than technical: this is a 30 ECTS thesis for currently enrolled final-year master's students, he graduated in May 2026, and the stated start is Spring 2026, already past. It belongs on the project backlog, not the application list.
